description: Optional richer source material for the FDE assessment. All people, organizations and statements are fictional. No production records or independently verified credentials are included.
usage: Use alongside the four existing JSON files; do not replace them.
Candidate IDs C1-C4, profile IDs R01-R12 and job references match the original packet.
Full resumes are expanded renditions of the original extracts, not independent corroborating evidence or later candidate updates. rendition_of identifies the original source.
New notes preserve unresolved gaps and conflicts. A note repeating a candidate message is not independent verification; related_source_ids identify that lineage.
All supplemental records belong to the 18:00 snapshot. Replay EV-JOB-904 at 18:05 and EV-C1-NEW at 18:10 from the original files only after loading that snapshot.
Missing details remain unspecified. This packet supplies neither expected rankings nor a required matching architecture.
Discovery notes are fictional exercise context, not verbatim customer statements or universal business policy.

notes.body: Alex's latest message mentions Spokane, December 1 and $2,400 for forty hours. The older Oregon-only preference is still visible in the ATS. I have not updated those structured fields. The résumé on file describes home-health work; the old ATS skills list is shorter.

I asked Blair to describe any home visits, start-of-care documentation and Homecare Homebase use. No response to those questions is recorded yet. The résumé describes outpatient work. My earlier positive impression of the hospital and school was not a verification of those specific skills.

Casey says the current assignment runs Monday through Wednesday and offers the two Dayton day shifts. R3 owns the placement. I have not independently checked the placement schedule or approved any additional-work outreach.

Drew's latest message declines both December dates and asks for no job contact until January 15. The older contact_allowed field still says true. I have not changed that field yet. No new availability confirmation was received.

My November 5 note reflects the facility conversation: one year of home-health experience is acceptable; OASIS is still needed for start-of-care visits; Homecare Homebase can be trained. The feed has not yet been edited. The $2,450 figure is candidate pay for forty hours, not the facility bill rate. I have no confirmed exception to the December 1 start.

The request is for both December 5 and December 6, 07:00–19:00 in Dayton local time. I have not confirmed whether the facility would accept someone for only one day. The posting allows consideration of other boards with ATLS, ACLS, PALS and BLS; no individual candidate has been approved by the facility.

The candidate's update says three years of home-health work. The profile names one employer from May 2025. I asked for earlier employer names and dates; they are not recorded yet. I have not corrected the profile's history.

The candidate says they have not used Homecare Homebase, although the imported profile lists it. The update also says two years in home health. I have asked for a dated work-history breakdown; no reply is recorded yet.

discovery_notes.text: I use notes to understand the actual setting. A physical-therapist label alone does not tell me whether somebody has done home visits or outpatient work.
A facility sometimes clarifies a requirement before the vendor feed is updated. We need to agree who can approve those changes and how the recruiter sees the source.
Placed does not tell me which days are occupied. I need the shift dates, times and the candidate's current response before discussing additional work.
Show me what you used from the résumé, notes and messages. When two sources disagree, I want to inspect them and understand what needs a follow-up.
Recommendations may need to go to the recruiter who owns the relationship. Finding a match does not settle permission to contact or submit someone.

Different divisions may prioritize different things. We have not agreed the configuration controls, score thresholds, source-precedence rules or freshness windows. Ask which decisions matter for your proposed workflow.
